title: phase-stratified-seqblast-runner-and-stitch-reporting-pipeline
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Add a new phase-stratified workload runner (seqblast) and a stitch-based reporting pipeline that produces per-phase latency heatmaps and kernel attribution summaries. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: existing workload runners sample sequences uniformly and fail to capture phase-skew behaviors observed in customer traffic (e.g., bursts of long sequences interleaved with many short ones). This PR adds a phase-stratified workload generator (seqblast) that explicitly models sequence-length phases and produces deterministic, seedable workloads suitable for profiling and regression comparisons. The change also includes a lightweight "stitch" reporter that correlates per-token latency deltas with kernel selection boundaries so we can attribute tail spikes to specific execution kernels or cache effects.
Changes: - bench/runners/seqblast_runner.go: new Go runner implementing configurable phase distributions, phase-duration schedules, and weighted sequence priming to emulate KV-cache warmup/decay patterns. Supports deterministic seed, per-phase warmup windows, and per-sequence metadata tags. - bench/reporters/stitch_reporter.py: Python reporter that ingests runner traces and runtime kernel telemetry, stitches token-level timing across phase boundaries, and emits a compact CSV plus JSON summary for downstream visualization. - configs/profiles/seqblast_profile.yaml: example profiles for short-burst, long-tail, and mixed-phase workloads used by CI and perf lab. - tests/bench/seqblast_integ.test: integration harness that runs seqblast against a local perf-canary endpoint and asserts steady-state token rates and KV cache hit behavior. - docs/benchmarking/seqblast.md: design notes, recommended profile parameters, and examples for reproducing customer-like phase-skew traffic.
Checklist: - [x] Implement runner and reporter - [x] Unit tests for phase scheduler and seed determinism - [x] Integration test against local perf-canary - [x] Basic docs with example profiles - [x] CI pipeline updated to include a lightweight smoke run
Impact and rationale: This gives us a middle-ground workload between synthetic uniform sequence samplers and heavy session replayers. Seqblast is intentionally deterministic so benchmarks are reproducible across perf lab runs and worker hardware. The stitch reporter surfaces short-lived kernel transitions that previously required manual flamegraph comparisons. Related: ENG-1124 (phase-aware latency investigation), ENG-1188 (KV cache decay tuning).
Follow-ups: - Add an ingestion path from stitch_reporter output into the telemetry warehouse (scheduled job) - Add a visualization dashboard showing per-phase p50/p95/p99 heatmaps - Experiment with adaptive phase widths driven by live request traces
Notes on CI: the first CI run failed due to linter warnings in the new Python reporter; fixed in commit 3. The final CI status is green. Merge method: squash and merge.
commits_summary: 1) initial seqblast runner implementation, phase scheduler, deterministic seed support
2) add stitch reporter and CSV/JSON serializers; initial unit tests
3) fix Python linting, tighten integration test thresholds, add docs and example profiles
